introduction: Prince Hamlet mourns his father while Denmark's new king, his uncle Claudius, celebrates marriage to Hamlet's mother. A disturbing apparition brings private grief into contact with the possibility of a concealed crime. Watched by courtiers and unsure whom to trust, Hamlet must judge appearances, test testimony and decide what action the dead can demand of the living. The tragedy follows the cost of revenge through a family and a kingdom where love, conscience and political survival become entangled.

fullSynopsis.text: At Elsinore, soldiers and Horatio encounter a Ghost resembling Denmark's dead king. Prince Hamlet already despairs over his father's death and his mother Gertrude's swift marriage to Claudius, the dead man's brother and successor. The Ghost tells Hamlet that Claudius murdered him by pouring poison into his ear and demands revenge, while forbidding action against Gertrude. Hamlet swears to remember, binds his companions to secrecy and announces that he may adopt an appearance of madness. Meanwhile, Claudius seeks to restrain the Norwegian prince Fortinbras's threatened attempt to recover lost territory.

Polonius and his departing son Laertes warn Ophelia against trusting Hamlet's courtship, and she obeys her father's order to refuse his visits and letters. After she reports Hamlet's alarming behaviour, Polonius attributes it to frustrated love. Claudius recruits Hamlet's old companions Rosencrantz and Guildenstern to discover his trouble, but Hamlet makes them admit that they were sent for. Visiting actors stir his shame at his own inaction. Doubting whether the Ghost may be a devil exploiting his melancholy, he arranges a performance resembling the alleged murder to test Claudius's conscience.

While Claudius and Polonius watch secretly, Hamlet harshly rejects Ophelia, leaving the King convinced that love does not explain the danger. Hamlet and Horatio then observe Claudius during the play; when the staged poison enters the sleeping ruler's ear, Claudius stops the performance. Alone afterward, he admits his brother's murder but cannot repent while retaining its rewards. Hamlet finds him kneeling and delays killing him because he supposes prayer might send him to heaven. In Gertrude's chamber, Hamlet stabs a hidden listener, discovering Polonius rather than the King. The Ghost returns, invisible to Gertrude, to renew the command for revenge.

Claudius sends Hamlet to England with Rosencrantz and Guildenstern carrying a secret order for his execution. Passing Fortinbras's army bound for Poland, Hamlet again rebukes his own delay. Ophelia's grief over her father's death appears in distracted songs and broken speech. Laertes returns with armed supporters demanding justice, but Claudius redirects his anger toward Hamlet. Letters unexpectedly announce Hamlet's return after a pirate encounter. Claudius and Laertes plan a fencing match with an unblunted, poisoned sword and a poisoned cup as a second means of murder. Gertrude then reports Ophelia's drowning after a branch broke over a brook.

Back with Horatio, Hamlet meditates on mortality in a graveyard and recognizes the skull of Yorick, the jester he knew as a child. Ophelia's funeral arrives with restricted rites because her death is considered doubtful; Hamlet discovers whose grave it is and grapples with Laertes in a contest of grief. Later he tells Horatio that he found Claudius's execution order at sea and replaced it with instructions to kill its bearers, sealing the substitution with his father's signet. He regrets his behaviour toward Laertes and accepts the proposed match despite an ominous feeling, speaking instead of readiness and providence.

Hamlet asks Laertes's pardon before they fence. Gertrude drinks from the poisoned cup despite Claudius's warning. Laertes wounds Hamlet with the poisoned weapon; in the ensuing scuffle their swords change hands, and Hamlet wounds Laertes. As Gertrude dies identifying the drink as poison, Laertes exposes the plot and blames the King. Hamlet stabs Claudius with the poisoned sword and forces him to drink. Laertes asks for mutual forgiveness and dies; Hamlet answers with a wish for his pardon in heaven. Hamlet prevents Horatio from following him in death, charging his friend to tell his story, then dies himself after giving his voice to Fortinbras as Denmark's next ruler.

Fortinbras arrives from Poland with English ambassadors, who report Rosencrantz and Guildenstern dead. Horatio undertakes to explain the catastrophe before the court. Fortinbras asserts his claim to the kingdom and orders Hamlet borne away with a soldier's honours, as the Danish royal family's collapse passes into public history.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: A Ghost in the dead King's armour appears to the watch and Horatio as Denmark prepares against young Fortinbras's territorial claims. At court, Claudius combines mourning with celebration of his marriage to Gertrude, sends envoys to Norway, permits Laertes to return to France and urges Hamlet to remain in Denmark. Hamlet privately condemns the hasty marriage and wishes his own life could end. Horatio's report draws him to the night watch. Elsewhere, Laertes and Polonius warn Ophelia that Hamlet's affection cannot safely promise marriage; she agrees to stop receiving him. Hamlet follows the Ghost despite his friends' fears. It identifies itself as his father, accuses Claudius of murder by poison and demands revenge, while leaving Gertrude to heaven and conscience. Hamlet swears obedience, exacts secrecy from Horatio and Marcellus, and warns that he may put on an eccentric or mad manner.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Polonius sends Reynaldo to investigate Laertes in Paris by indirect questioning and carefully limited slander. Ophelia then describes a disturbing, silent visit from Hamlet after she rejected his letters and access. Polonius concludes that love has driven him mad. Claudius and Gertrude summon Rosencrantz and Guildenstern to find the cause of Hamlet's altered behaviour. Envoys report that Norway has redirected Fortinbras against Poland and requests passage through Denmark. Polonius produces Hamlet's love letter and proposes secretly observing him with Ophelia. Hamlet mocks Polonius, recognizes his friends' mission and describes the loss of pleasure that darkens his world. The arrival of players briefly animates him. A player's tears over Hecuba make him reproach his own delay, but he also distrusts the Ghost's origin. He commissions a play resembling his father's murder to seek firmer evidence in Claudius's reaction.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Claudius and Polonius spy on Hamlet's meeting with Ophelia after his meditation on life, death and the fear of what follows. His harsh rejection convinces Claudius to send him to England. Hamlet coaches the actors and recruits Horatio to watch the King during the performance. The staged poisoning makes Claudius rise and end the play, confirming Hamlet's suspicion. Claudius privately confesses the murder, yet cannot relinquish its rewards or achieve true repentance. Hamlet sees him kneeling and spares him for the moment, believing death at prayer might save his soul. In Gertrude's chamber, Polonius hides behind the arras. Hamlet stabs through it when he hears a cry, killing the wrong man. He condemns Gertrude's marriage; the Ghost appears to him again, but she sees nothing. Hamlet urges her to repent and conceal his feigned madness, then drags Polonius's body away.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Gertrude reports Polonius's killing to Claudius, who accelerates Hamlet's removal. Hamlet evades questions about the body before revealing its location. Claudius sends him toward England, secretly requesting his immediate death. Hamlet encounters a captain of Fortinbras's army and contrasts its willingness to fight for worthless land with his own delayed revenge. At Elsinore, Ophelia's disordered songs and symbolic flowers expose her grief. Laertes storms the palace with supporters, demanding an account of his father's death; Claudius persuades him to investigate with him. Hamlet's letters report that pirates separated him from his ship and that he is returning, while his companions continue toward England. Claudius and Laertes devise a sham sporting match: Laertes will use an unblunted blade coated in poison, with poisoned wine held in reserve. Gertrude interrupts with the report that Ophelia fell into a brook and drowned.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Gravediggers dispute Ophelia's entitlement to Christian burial. Hamlet's conversation with one, including his recognition of Yorick's skull, turns death from abstraction to familiar remains. At Ophelia's funeral he clashes with Laertes over their love and grief. He later tells Horatio how he replaced Claudius's order for his execution with one condemning Rosencrantz and Guildenstern. Accepting the fencing wager despite unease, Hamlet asks Laertes's forgiveness. Gertrude drinks the poisoned wine; Laertes wounds Hamlet, then is wounded with the same blade after a sword exchange. Gertrude dies, and Laertes reveals the plot. Hamlet kills Claudius with sword and poisoned drink. Laertes dies seeking mutual pardon. Hamlet answers him, then charges Horatio to survive and explain before dying himself. Fortinbras arrives alongside ambassadors confirming the two courtiers' deaths, asserts his claim and orders military honours for Hamlet while Horatio prepares a public account.
